note: Criterion medians for the hot benches named in the P0/P4 acceptance lines. Criterion's own default protocol (3 s warm-up, 100 samples); the statistic is the median point estimate from target/criterion/<id>/new/estimates.json, which is what scripts/check-perf-budgets.sh compares. Do not mix in mean-based numbers: the 2026-09-18 acceptance run recorded means, and a mean/median pair is not a controlled comparison.
host: macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Apple M4 Pro, rustc 1.98.0

budgets.comment: The bench with no headroom: +9.9% against the pre-2.0 figure when this budget was written. A real regression here is the thing the budget exists to catch.
MOTION-GAP A9: a 1000-segment self-drawn chart, full software frame (encode + flatten + stroke + scanline rasterise). This is the worst case the flat-scene walk absorbs with no damage to skip.
MOTION-GAP A9: the 10k-segment extreme. Scales linearly with the 1k figure (~8.4 us/segment), which is the shape evidence that nothing per-node is superlinear.
MOTION-GAP A9: 1000 filled discs, area-dominated rasterisation, ~2 us per disc at r=6.

MOTION-GAP A9: 1000 filled rounded rects (40x24, r=8) — the shape a card, button or list row is. Each is a small filled path; heavier than circles_1k because the rounded corners flatten to more segments.
